# BITS

> BITS is a community for sharing, reusing and discovering small code snippets, with public profiles, groups, a language and dependency catalog, and a searchable command box.

## Core pages

- [BITS homepage](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/): Introduces the snippet-sharing community and provides search, example snippets, catalog shortcuts and site-wide navigation.
- [Languages](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/languages): Public catalog of programming languages, with links to language detail pages and snippets that use each language.
- [Dependencies](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/dependencies): Public catalog of frameworks, libraries, tools and runtimes used by shared snippets.
- [Search](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/search): Searches public snippets and groups by title, description, language, tags and dependencies.
- [Changelog](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/changelog): Newest-first timeline of published BITS product updates, new features and fixes.
- [Request a catalog entry](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/request): Signed-in form for requesting a missing programming language or dependency.
- [Extended AI reference](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/llms-full.txt): Detailed description of BITS features, content rules, documentation, public routes and developer integration.

## Documentation

- [BITS documentation](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs): Bilingual English and Chinese user documentation covering accounts, snippets, groups, discovery and privacy.
- [Getting started](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/getting-started): Explains what BITS is, what users can do and how to configure a username and public profile.
- [Creating snippets](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/snippets): Describes the three-step editor, snippet fields, generated URLs, tags, dependencies and visibility.
- [Editing and deleting](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/editing): Explains editable fields and URL names, redirects from old links, soft deletion and administrator restoration.
- [Groups](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/groups): Covers creating groups, assigning snippets and how group pages and deletion behave.
- [Search and the command box](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/search): Documents slash commands, keyword matching and catalog-aware search.
- [Your profile](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/profile): Explains profile content, owner-only actions, private tabs, ordering, contribution activity and followers.
- [Copy and fork](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/copy-fork): Covers share links, copy counts, snippet forks and group forks while preserving source attribution.
- [Visibility and privacy](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/visibility): Defines public, unlisted and private access, search visibility and 404 behavior for unauthorised visitors.
- [Language and dependency requests](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/requests): Explains catalog requests, moderation, status tracking and duplicate-name limits.
- [Changelog documentation](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/changelog): Describes the public release timeline and how published updates are loaded.
- [FAQ](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/faq): Answers common questions about publishing, URL suffixes, 404 responses, deleting and restoring content.

## Developer platform

- [Developer platform](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/developer): Entry point for BITS applications, OAuth services and API Keys.
- [Apps documentation](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/developer/apps): Explains App identity and how an application connects to an OAuth service. API Keys are account-level and do not require an App.
- [OAuth documentation](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/developer/oauth): Documents authorization code flow, PKCE, refresh tokens, device flow, scopes, userinfo and revocation.
- [API Keys documentation](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/developer/api-keys): Explains scoped API Keys, permissions, expiry, one-time display, last use and revocation.
- [Open API v1 documentation](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/developer/open-api): Documents API-key authentication, endpoints, pagination, permissions and rate limits for managing owned snippets and groups.
- [OpenAPI specification](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/openapi.json): Machine-readable OpenAPI 3.1 specification for `/api/v1`. The same document is served at `/api/v1/openapi.json`.

## Product definition

BITS is a lightweight code-sharing product. Its primary objects are reusable snippets and folders called groups. A snippet has one primary language, optional dependencies and tags, a title, description, code body and visibility setting. Public profiles and catalog pages connect snippets to authors, technologies and discovery paths. Developers can create Apps for OAuth integrations and account-level API Keys for server-to-server Open API access. BITS is oriented toward small, reusable examples rather than full repository hosting.

## Key facts

- Canonical site: https://bits.micropue.com.cn
- Content visibility: public, unlisted and private; private content and unauthorised access return 404.
- Public discovery: language and dependency catalog pages, public profiles, search and the slash command box.
- Accounts: email-code, GitHub and passkey sign-in are supported; a username is required before publishing public or unlisted content.
- URLs: profiles use `/{username}`; content uses `/{username}/{slug}`. In the website editor, a snippet URL name is read-only and follows Name. The Open API can rename snippet and group slugs explicitly, and supported old public links redirect to the new address.
- Forks: copying a public snippet opens a confirmation flow where the signed-in user can edit the new URL name and choose private, unlisted or public visibility before creating the copy.
- Developer access: Apps can use OAuth 2.0 with `read:user` and `read:email` scopes. Accounts can keep up to 50 Apps and 50 OAuth services. Account-level API Keys use scoped permissions, are not tied to an App, and each account can retain up to 50 active keys.
- Open API: `/api/v1` uses scoped API Keys and can manage only the owner's snippets and groups, never account or security settings. Writes require `Content-Type: application/json`. Reads are limited to 120 requests per minute per key and writes to 30 per minute per key, with account-wide caps of 240 reads and 60 writes per minute across all keys. Snippet lists omit code bodies; single-snippet responses include them. Errors use RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`.
- Sitemap: https://bits.micropue.com.cn/sitemap.xml
- Last updated: 2026-11-27
